problems: The first frame does not clearly read as 1893 because the large red number is caught in a messy transition.
The hook is interesting, but the opening holds too long with almost no new information.
The story is clear eventually, but each phrase is stretched over too many seconds.
The food image does not support the tomato debate strongly enough and looks like a random recipe photo.
Important explanatory text is sometimes pale grey during reveals and low-contrast against the beige background.
There is no visual tomato hero moment, no Supreme Court/courtroom cue beyond text, and no RecipeFix/product connection inside the video.

fixes: Make the cover a clean static hook: 'In 1893, the Supreme Court ruled a tomato was a vegetable.' with a strong tomato visual.
Cut the runtime to 12-15 seconds; combine beats instead of revealing one word at a time.
Open with the conflict immediately: 'Fruit was tax-free. Vegetables were taxed 10%. So an importer sued.'
Replace the generic pasta/shrimp image with a close-up tomato crate, market illustration, vintage produce label, or courtroom/tomato collage.
Increase contrast on all grey text or avoid showing unreadably faded text during transitions.
Remove or explain the tiny top-right icon if it is not a brand mark.
Add an on-video brand bridge at the end, e.g. 'Fruit or veg, RecipeFix adapts the steps to how you cook.'
End with a sharper final card or CTA, not just the source bar lingering.
